plants.name: Tradescantia zebrina
plants.tip: Pinch every stem back hard in spring. Left alone it goes bald at the crown and trails bare string.
plants.colour: Two silver bands on olive-purple leaves, deep magenta underside

plants.name: Tradescantia zebrina 'Purpusii'
plants.tip: The purple is a sun pigment. In a dim spot it fades to bronze-green and stays that way.
plants.colour: Unbanded bronze to deep purple, faintly hairy

plants.name: Tradescantia zebrina 'Quadricolor'
plants.tip: Cut out any all-green shoots as they appear, or they will outgrow and swamp the striped ones.
plants.colour: Green, silver, cream and pink striping over a purple underside

plants.name: Tradescantia zebrina 'Silver Plus'
plants.tip: Broad silver means less chlorophyll and slower growth. Do not push it with extra feed.
plants.colour: Almost wholly silver leaf with narrow green margins, purple beneath

plants.name: Tradescantia zebrina 'Violet Hill'
plants.tip: Grow it bright to keep the near-black colour. Reverted green growth should be cut out at the node.
plants.colour: Very dark violet leaves with a faint silver sheen

plants.name: Tradescantia fluminensis
plants.tip: It roots from any node that touches damp compost. Trim it back rather than letting it sprawl and rot.
plants.colour: Plain glossy mid-green with purple-tinged stems

plants.name: Tradescantia fluminensis 'Tricolor'
plants.tip: The pink only holds in bright light. Remove reverted green stems, as reverted growth never comes back.
plants.colour: Green and cream stripes flushed pink at the leaf edge

plants.name: Tradescantia fluminensis 'Albovittata'
plants.tip: Grows faster than the pink forms and reverts less. Pinch tips monthly to keep it dense.
plants.colour: Mid-green with clean white longitudinal stripes

plants.name: Tradescantia fluminensis 'Quicksilver'
plants.tip: Vigorous and quick to go leggy. Cut it back by half in spring and root the trimmings in the same pot.
plants.colour: Broad white and grey-green stripes on a green ground

plants.name: Tradescantia fluminensis 'Maiden's Blush'
plants.tip: New growth carries the pink; old leaves green over. Keep pinching to force fresh coloured shoots.
plants.colour: Cream and green leaves with strong pink on the new growth

plants.name: Tradescantia pallida 'Purpurea'
plants.tip: Wants more direct sun than the rest of the genus. Too little and the purple turns dull green.
plants.colour: Deep violet-purple lance-shaped leaves, pale pink flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia pallida 'Pink Stripes'
plants.tip: The stripes come out on new leaves in bright light. Shade gives plain purple growth instead.
plants.colour: Purple leaves streaked with pink and pale green

plants.name: Tradescantia spathacea
plants.tip: It holds water in the leaf bases, so let the top half of the pot dry before watering again.
plants.colour: Stiff green rosette with deep purple undersides

plants.name: Tradescantia spathacea 'Tricolor'
plants.tip: Water at the compost, not into the rosette, or the packed leaf bases will rot.
plants.colour: Green and cream striped leaves with pink flushing, purple beneath

plants.name: Tradescantia spathacea 'Sitara's Gold'
plants.tip: The yellow burns in direct sun. Bright indirect light keeps it gold rather than bleached.
plants.colour: Yellow-gold and green striped leaves, purple undersides

plants.name: Tradescantia spathacea 'Vittata'
plants.tip: A dwarf form that offsets from the base. Split the clump every second spring to keep it tidy.
plants.colour: Compact rosette striped cream and green, purple below

plants.name: Tradescantia sillamontana
plants.tip: Treat it as a succulent. The felted leaves mark if watered overhead, so water the compost only.
plants.colour: Grey-green leaves under dense white wool, magenta flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Nanouk'
plants.tip: Thicker stemmed than most and slower to trail. Bright light keeps the pink; shade turns it green.
plants.colour: Broad green leaves striped cream and bright pink, purple beneath

plants.name: Tradescantia cerinthoides 'Variegata'
plants.tip: Sturdier and more upright than the trailing kinds. Cut back any plain green reversion at once.
plants.colour: Thick green leaves striped cream, undersides deep maroon

plants.name: Tradescantia chrysophylla 'Baby Bunny Bellies'
plants.tip: The soft leaves scorch in direct sun and crisp in dry air. Keep it out of the path of radiators.
plants.colour: Velvety olive-green leaves with rich burgundy undersides

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Bubblegum'
plants.tip: Colour is light-driven. In a dim corner the pink drains away and the stems stretch between leaves.
plants.colour: Green leaves washed pink and cream, magenta undersides

plants.name: Tradescantia virginiana
plants.tip: Each flower lasts a morning. Shear the whole clump back after the first flush and it repeats.
plants.colour: Grassy green leaves, three-petalled violet-blue flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia ohiensis
plants.tip: Tougher and more drought-tolerant than the garden hybrids, but it flops in rich soil and shade.
plants.colour: Blue-grey waxy foliage, pale blue to purple flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Sweet Kate'
plants.tip: The gold foliage scorches in hard midday sun. Morning sun with afternoon shade keeps it clean.
plants.colour: Bright chartreuse-gold leaves with deep blue flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Concord Grape'
plants.tip: Cut it to the ground when the foliage tires in midsummer. Fresh leaves and a second flush follow.
plants.colour: Blue-grey foliage with rich purple-grape flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Zwanenburg Blue'
plants.tip: Large flowered and inclined to flop. Give it a support ring early rather than staking it later.
plants.colour: Green strap leaves, large deep blue flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Osprey'
plants.tip: Deadhead the spent stems to stop it seeding about, as seedlings come nothing like the parent.
plants.colour: White flowers with a fluffy blue central boss

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Bilberry Ice'
plants.tip: Keep the soil moist. Drought turns the lower leaves yellow and it will not green up again.
plants.colour: Pale lilac-white petals with a deeper violet centre stripe

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Innocence'
plants.tip: The white shows every mark, so shear off tired stems as soon as the first flush finishes.
plants.colour: Pure white flowers with yellow stamens, mid-green leaves

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Red Grape'
plants.tip: Flowers most freely in sun with moisture at the root. Dry shade gives leaves and almost nothing else.
plants.colour: Deep rose-magenta flowers over green foliage

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Little Doll'
plants.tip: A compact form that suits a pot. Divide it every third spring or the middle of the clump dies out.
plants.colour: Pale lavender-blue flowers on a short tidy clump

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Karminglut'
plants.tip: Cut back by half after flowering. Left uncut it splays open and shows bare stem at the centre.
plants.colour: Carmine-red flowers against grey-green leaves

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Charlotte'
plants.tip: Wants steady moisture and will wilt fast in a small pot. Mulch the crown rather than feeding harder.
plants.colour: Soft pink flowers with paler centres

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Purple Dome'
plants.tip: Free flowering over a long season. Remove seed heads weekly and it keeps producing buds.
plants.colour: Rich purple flowers on a dense rounded clump

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Pauline'
plants.tip: Taller than most, so plant it where neighbours can hold it up. Staking singly looks wrong.
plants.colour: Pale mauve-pink flowers with prominent stamens

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Blue Stone'
plants.tip: Happier in damp ground than most perennials. It will take a border edge that stays wet in winter.
plants.colour: Clear mid-blue flowers over narrow green leaves

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Danielle'
plants.tip: Shear to the ground in midsummer once it looks tired, and it returns fresh for a late flush.
plants.colour: White flowers held above upright green foliage

plants.name: Tradescantia 'J.C. Weguelin'
plants.tip: One of the largest flowered, and it needs the moisture to match. Never let the clump dry out.
plants.colour: Large soft china-blue flowers

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Leonora'
plants.tip: Reliable and upright. Divide in spring rather than autumn, as new divisions rot in cold wet soil.
plants.colour: Violet-blue flowers over grey-green strap leaves

plants.name: Tradescantia 'Purewell Giant'
plants.tip: Vigorous and wide spreading. Give it half a metre or it will lean over smaller neighbours.
plants.colour: Deep carmine-purple flowers on a tall clump
